Q: java.lang.ClassFormatError: Duplicate method name "rendersContent" with signature "(Lorg.jooq.Context;)Z" in class file TestSchema A:

I got rid of the runtime error by changing the object TestSchema into a regular class. Then I just had to change usages of the former object to instances of the class.

Q: Provisioning VMs with Terraform on vSphere A:

First of all, I agree with Marco and highly recommend using remote state for your scenario, as managing state files locally (especially deleting them) can lead to inconsistencies and is not safe for long-lived resources. To keep things organized and maintainable, you should create a reusable Terraform module for your VM, and for each deployment, have a separate folder that uses this module. This way, the central logic stays in the module, and each deployment remains isolated.

To automate this, modify your script to accept a deployment name as an input parameter. Use this name both for naming the configuration folder and as part of the backend key during Terraform initialization. Each deployment folder should contain a minimal set of files: a main.tf that calls the central VM module, a variables.tf for input variables (you can create them from a template folder via script), and a .tfvars file with deployment-specific values. This ensures each deployment has its own state file and configuration, making administration straightforward and scalable as more teams request VMs. If you need even more flexibility, you can look into tools like Terragrunt, but this approach works well with plain Terraform too.
